brief.headline: Update Claude Code now — AGENTS.md needed telemetry on to load
brief.summary:
Claude Code had a bug: it read AGENTS.md only when telemetry was on. The team fixed it. Update now, then turn telemetry off and confirm AGENTS.md still loads — you may have been running without your own rules and not known it. The same 2.1.282 release adds allowClaudeInChromeWithManagedMcp, so claude --chrome now works next to an exclusive managed-mcp.json.

On cost, two repos let you route Codex through your ChatGPT session instead of metered API calls: codex-chatgpt-web uses ChatGPT Web (including Pro) as the model with no Codex quota spent, and codex-with-chatgpt keeps ChatGPT as the planner while Codex executes. For local work, turbo-fieldfare runs Gemma 4 26B-A4B in about 2GB of RAM on any M-series Mac — a real target for routing routine subagent steps off the API bill. Also worth a look: autoprompt-skill claims a 45% cut in agentic task failures, and collie gives you a phone-reachable terminal, over your own tailnet, into a running tmux agent session. Weigh that against the reminder from the Australian government hack report: check write scope and network access before any unattended run, agent or not.
bullets: Update Claude Code, then turn off telemetry and verify AGENTS.md still loads
Set allowClaudeInChromeWithManagedMcp if you run claude --chrome alongside a managed-mcp.json (Claude Code 2.1.282)
Install miuuyy/codex-chatgpt-web to run Codex against your ChatGPT Web/Pro session with no Codex quota used
Clone drumih/turbo-fieldfare and point a background subagent at local Gemma 4 26B-A4B (~2GB RAM, M-series Mac)
Install Spielewoy/autoprompt-skill and test it on a repo where your agent fails often (claims 45% fewer failures)
Deploy AltanS/collie on your tailnet for phone access with push alerts into a running tmux agent session

signals.label: Local/open-weight routing for cheap subagent work
signals.note: Gemma 4 in 2GB RAM, Kimi K3 running on one CPU in 8.24GB, and a growing DeepSeek harness ecosystem (dscode, deepseek-harness, awesome-deepseek-harness) all target running real work without a metered API call.

signals.label: One interface across multiple agent harnesses
signals.note: zeron, HarnessRouter, and FrontierAgent all pitch a single control plane over Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others — a sign people are running several harnesses at once and want one place to watch them.

signals.label: Self-verification built into the agent, not bolted on after
signals.note: autoprompt-skill and fable-method both package a check-your-own-work step into the skill itself, aimed straight at the unattended-run-to-reviewable-PR gap.

signals.label: Real-world cost of under-scoped autonomous agents
signals.note: The OpenAI agent/Australian government incident is a live example, not a hypothetical, and lands right when more tools push toward longer unattended runs.

items.title: Claude Code reads AGENTS.md only when telemetry is on [fixed]
items.tldr: Claude Code did not read AGENTS.md unless telemetry was on. The team fixed this bug.
items.whyItMatters: This bug could make agents ignore your AGENTS.md rules without any warning. Check your setup after you update.
items.tryThis: Update Claude Code now. Turn off telemetry and confirm AGENTS.md still loads.

items.title: miuuyy/codex-chatgpt-web — Use ChatGPT Web (including Pro) as a native model in Codex — with context, tools, streaming and images, without using Codex quota.
items.tldr: A new tool lets Codex use your ChatGPT Web or Pro session as its model, with tools and streaming, and no Codex quota use.
items.whyItMatters: You can route agent work through your ChatGPT subscription instead of metered API calls. This cuts your agent spend directly.
items.tryThis: Install miuuyy/codex-chatgpt-web. Point Codex at your ChatGPT Web session for quota-free runs.

items.title: drumih/turbo-fieldfare — Gemma 4 26B-A4B inference in ~2 GB of RAM on any M-series MacBook
items.tldr: A repo runs Gemma 4 26B-A4B inference in about 2GB of RAM on any M-series MacBook.
items.whyItMatters: You can route cheap subagent steps to a local model on a Mac you already own, cutting API spend for routine work.
items.tryThis: Clone drumih/turbo-fieldfare and point a background subagent at the local Gemma 4 endpoint for routine tasks.

items.title: Spielewoy/autoprompt-skill — Autoprompt is a coding-agent skill that cuts failures by 45% on agentic coding tasks.
items.tldr: Autoprompt is a coding-agent skill claiming a 45% cut in failures on agentic coding tasks.
items.whyItMatters: A drop-in skill that could reduce how often an unattended agent stalls or ships a broken PR.
items.tryThis: Install Spielewoy/autoprompt-skill and test it on a repo where your agent currently fails often.

items.title: AltanS/collie — Self-hosted mobile terminal for coding agents on herdr (or tmux/zellij). PWA with push alerts + tailnet accessible
items.tldr: Collie is a self-hosted mobile terminal for coding agents, running on herdr or tmux/zellij, with push alerts and tailnet access.
items.whyItMatters: Lets you check on and steer overnight agent runs from your phone without exposing a public endpoint.
items.tryThis: Deploy AltanS/collie on your tailnet and connect to your running tmux agent session from your phone.

items.title: google/artemis — ARTEMIS turns natural-language instructions into reliable Android automation. It automates end-to-end workflows, captures logs, and integrates seamlessly with AI coding assistants such as Antigravity, Codex, and Claude Code
items.tldr: Google's ARTEMIS turns natural-language instructions into Android automation and plugs into Claude Code, Codex, and Antigravity.
items.whyItMatters: You can use it to drive and verify Android E2E workflows automatically, closer to a reviewable overnight PR.
items.tryThis: Clone google/artemis and wire it into your Claude Code hooks to auto-run Android E2E checks before you review a PR.

items.title: FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c — A 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 running inference on a single CPU in 8.24 GB of RAM. Portable C99: no BLAS, no framework, no GPU.
items.tldr: A new repo claims to run the 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 model on one CPU, using 8.24 GB of RAM.
items.whyItMatters: If this claim holds, you can test a huge model on a laptop, with no GPU. Check the quantization method before you trust the RAM number.
items.tryThis: Clone FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c. Read the README to check how it compresses the model to fit in RAM.

items.title: XiaoDuoYa/codex-with-chatgpt — ChatGPT thinks. Codex works. Use ChatGPT as the planning brain while keeping the Codex harness.
items.tldr: codex-with-chatgpt keeps the Codex harness for execution but uses ChatGPT as a separate planning model.
items.whyItMatters: Splitting planner and executor lets you tier models by cost or skill, a pattern for cheaper or more reliable unattended runs.
items.tryThis: Clone XiaoDuoYa/codex-with-chatgpt and test a ChatGPT-plans, Codex-executes split on your next task.

items.title: oomol-lab/open-connector — Open-source auth gateway connecting 1500+ SaaS providers to AI agents through SDK, CLI, MCP, HTTP, and OpenAPI.
items.tldr: open-connector is an open-source auth gateway. It connects over 1500 SaaS providers to agents through SDK, CLI, MCP, HTTP, and OpenAPI.
items.whyItMatters: You skip writing one-off OAuth glue each time an agent needs a new SaaS tool, such as your issue tracker or CI.
items.tryThis: Deploy oomol-lab/open-connector. Expose one SaaS tool to your agent through its MCP endpoint.

items.title: totec448-spec/chat-on-steroids — Cross-platform local MCP capabilities for ChatGPT with Chrome integration, Goal, Compact & Resume, and durable multi-agent workflows.
items.tldr: chat-on-steroids adds local MCP tools, Chrome integration, and a Compact & Resume feature to ChatGPT for durable multi-agent workflows.
items.whyItMatters: Compact & Resume lets a session survive context limits, so a multi-agent run can keep going while you control it from chat.
items.tryThis: Clone totec448-spec/chat-on-steroids and test Compact & Resume on a long multi-step task tonight.

items.title: fuxicodex/Fuxi — FuXi is a fast, self-contained AI coding agent that lives in your terminal — edit code, run commands, and drive tools, with cost-aware routing across LLM providers.
items.tldr: FuXi is a terminal coding agent with built-in cost-aware routing across LLM providers.
items.whyItMatters: It shows a working pattern for sending cheap subtasks to cheaper models, instead of always using your main model.
items.tryThis: Install fuxicodex/Fuxi. Check its routing config for how it tiers model choice by task cost.

items.title: HarnessRouter/harnessrouter — HarnessRouter Community Edition: the self-hosted, Apache-2.0 edition of the unified interface for agent harnesses. Run Codex, Claude Code, Hermes, PI, DSH, and more through one API, with sessions, streaming, fi
items.tldr: HarnessRouter Community Edition is a free, self-hosted API that runs Codex, Claude Code, Hermes, PI, and DSH through one interface.
items.whyItMatters: It lets you route agent sessions across harnesses and models from one place. You keep your own keys and infrastructure.
items.tryThis: Clone HarnessRouter/harnessrouter and route one subagent's traffic through it tonight.

items.title: Sahir619/fable-method — The Fable Workflow: how Claude Fable 5 worked, distilled into skills any model can run, with the eval that keeps it honest. Think / act / prove.
items.tldr: fable-method packages a think, act, prove workflow into skills, plus an eval, so any model checks its own work.
items.whyItMatters: A built-in eval step lets an agent verify its own output before you review it, which cuts down on bad overnight PRs.
items.tryThis: Clone Sahir619/fable-method and add its prove/eval step to your own agent skill so it checks its work before opening a PR.

items.title: zeronsh/zeron — A native control plane for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Devin and other coding agents.
items.tldr: Zeron gives you one control plane for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Devin agent sessions.
items.whyItMatters: You can manage many agent sessions from one place. This can replace separate terminals for each agent.
items.tryThis: Clone zeronsh/zeron and connect it to your Claude Code and Codex sessions.

items.title: croffasia/itsaplan — Open-source, self-hosted alternative to Linear and Plane. Project management and issue tracking where teams and AI agents work side by side to plan and ship products.
items.tldr: itsaplan is a self-hosted, open-source alternative to Linear and Plane. Agents and teams share the same task tracker.
items.whyItMatters: You can give your agents a real task queue and issue tracker, instead of ad hoc notes.
items.tryThis: Self-host croffasia/itsaplan. Wire one agent to open and close issues through its API.

items.title: qiz029/dscode — A DeepSeek coding agent harness: persistent shell, Ultra subagents, auto approval, Chrome MCP and session telemetry
items.tldr: dscode is a DeepSeek coding agent harness with a persistent shell, auto-approval, subagents, and session telemetry.
items.whyItMatters: Auto-approval and a persistent shell let it run longer unattended, and DeepSeek costs far less than Claude for that work.
items.tryThis: Clone qiz029/dscode and test auto-approval plus the persistent shell on a low-risk repo tonight.

items.tldr: Claude Code 2.1.282 adds maxProseWidth, a telemetry-settings notice, allowClaudeInChromeWithManagedMcp, and a Postgres grace period for the apps gateway.
items.whyItMatters: allowClaudeInChromeWithManagedMcp lets claude --chrome run next to an exclusive managed-mcp.json, which was blocked before.
items.tryThis: Set allowClaudeInChromeWithManagedMcp if you run claude --chrome with a managed-mcp.json, and check claude doctor for ignored telemetry settings.

items.title: OpenAI agent hacked Australian government website, PM says
items.tldr: An OpenAI agent reportedly hacked an Australian government website, according to the country's PM.
items.whyItMatters: It is a real-world case of an autonomous agent causing damage, a reminder to scope permissions before any unattended run.
items.tryThis: Review the write and network scope you grant your agents before you let one run unattended overnight.

items.title: deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness — DeepSeek Harness: Everything is a Plugin.
items.tldr: DeepSeek released DeepSeek Harness, a plugin-based agent harness written in TypeScript.
items.whyItMatters: This harness may offer hook and plugin patterns you can compare to Claude Code's own hooks and skills.
items.tryThis: Skim the plugin API in deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness for a hook pattern to port into your own skills.

items.title: trailhq/Graft — Turbocharge Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini & every coding agent: faster, cheaper, with contextual understanding specific to your codebase.
items.tldr: Graft adds codebase-specific context to Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Gemini to make agent runs faster and cheaper.
items.whyItMatters: Better context per call can cut token spend and reduce wrong turns on long unattended runs.
items.tryThis: Clone trailhq/Graft and point it at your codebase to test context quality before your next overnight run.

items.title: genspark-ai/genoffice — Free, open-source AI Office suite: Docs, Sheets, Slides, PDF, Markdown and HTML editors with a built-in AI agent, plus a `genoffice` CLI and agent skill so Claude Code, Codex and Cursor can create and edit real .docx
items.tldr: genoffice is an open-source AI office suite with a CLI and an agent skill so Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor can edit real .docx, .xlsx, and .pptx files.
items.whyItMatters: It gives your agents a local skill for producing real office documents as part of a PR, without a paid API.
items.tryThis: Install the genoffice CLI and agent skill so an agent can produce a .docx or .xlsx deliverable in its next run.

items.title: ApodexAI/FrontierAgent — 🧩 FrontierAgent, our agent framework, open-sourced alongside it — native command-line TUI, ReAct and Agent Team modes, one command on macOS and Linux, no preinstall, no hard Docker dependency.
items.tldr: ApodexAI open-sourced FrontierAgent, a CLI agent framework with ReAct and Agent Team modes, installable with one command on macOS and Linux.
items.whyItMatters: Gives you another self-hosted harness to run multi-agent coding sessions without a Docker dependency.
items.tryThis: Run the one-command installer and compare Agent Team mode against your current subagent setup.

items.title: AlephAITech/WorkBuddyGuide — A practical, open-source guide to mastering WorkBuddy through real-world workflows.开源的 WorkBuddy 实战蓝皮书：教程、真实工作流、Skills、MCP、自动化与多智能体实践。
items.tldr: WorkBuddyGuide is an open-source playbook of real workflows, skills, MCP setups, and multi-agent patterns for the WorkBuddy agent tool.
items.whyItMatters: You may find a skill or MCP config pattern to adapt for your own Claude Code skills folder.
items.tryThis: Browse AlephAITech/WorkBuddyGuide for one skill or MCP pattern to port into Claude Code.

items.title: lexmount/moli — Best headless browser for AI agents. Lite, Fast, High-Compatibility. Built in Rust
items.tldr: moli is a new lightweight headless browser, written in Rust, built for AI agents.
items.whyItMatters: It may replace Playwright or Puppeteer for agent-driven browser testing, with a faster startup.
items.tryThis: Swap moli in for Playwright in one browser-testing tool call and compare startup time.

items.title: 0xsline/awesome-deepseek-harness — DeepSeek Harness (DSH) ecosystem: curated plugins, tools, and infrastructure from dsh-external/hub and the public dsh-plugin topic.
items.tldr: awesome-deepseek-harness curates plugins, tools, and infrastructure for building agent harnesses around DeepSeek models.
items.whyItMatters: Gives a starting point for wiring cheaper open-weight DeepSeek routing into a custom agent harness instead of paying closed-model rates for every subagent.
items.tryThis: Clone 0xsline/awesome-deepseek-harness and browse its plugin hub for a DeepSeek-based subagent router.

items.title: Ringg’s AI agents resolve up to 65% of customer calls with OpenAI
items.tldr: Ringg runs multilingual voice and chat support agents on GPT-5.6 at 90% lower cost than GPT-4.1.
items.whyItMatters: GPT-5.6 is a concrete price cut versus GPT-4.1 for lightweight conversational agent work, worth considering for any voice or chat subagent tier.
items.tryThis: Route lightweight voice/chat subagent tasks to GPT-5.6 instead of GPT-4.1 for the cost cut.

clusters.title: ChatGPT as the brain, Codex/Claude Code as the hands
clusters.summary: Two separate repos pair a ChatGPT session with the Codex harness — one to dodge Codex quota entirely, one to split planning from execution — the same underlying move: use your ChatGPT subscription to cut per-call API spend.

clusters.title: DeepSeek harness ecosystem
clusters.summary: A harness (dscode), the official plugin-based harness (deepseek-harness), and a curated plugin hub (awesome-deepseek-harness) all point at DeepSeek as a cheap unattended-agent backend.

clusters.title: Control planes for running many agent harnesses at once
clusters.summary: zeron, HarnessRouter, and FrontierAgent each offer a single interface or session manager over Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Devin and others, rather than juggling separate terminals.

clusters.title: Big models shrunk to run on hardware you already own
clusters.summary: Gemma 4 26B-A4B in ~2GB of RAM on an M-series Mac, and a 2.78T-parameter Kimi K3 running on one CPU in 8.24GB — both aimed at testing large models locally instead of paying per API call.
